data.name: Erminio
data.gender_notes: Erminio is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin name Herminius, Erminio means 'Soldier of Mercury'. In Roman mythology, Mercury was the god of commerce, wealth, and travel. The name Erminio carries the meaning “Soldier of Mercury” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Erminio usually hope their child will grow to embody soldier of mercury and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, adaptability, and agility in spiritual pursuits.
data.etymology: Erminio belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soldier of Mercury.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Erminio total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Erminio has a rich cultural history, symbolizing strength, bravery, and warrior spirit. It is a name associated with leadership, power, and the military. Particularly significant in European cultures, it is a name that warms the listener's heart with images of courage and valour.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Erminio lies in its association with Mercury, the Roman god of communication, trade, and travel. Erminio's name is a reminder of the importance of these aspects in our lives – the ability to communicate effectively, the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom, and the journey toward personal growth. It can inspire its bearer to be a messenger of hope, compassion, and understanding in the world. In a broader sense, it can also serve as a reminder of the importance of staying curious and open-minded in our spiritual journey, just as Mercury was always moving, connecting the different aspects of the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Erminio, derived from the Germanic name Ermen- ("all, entire, whole") and wald ("rule, power, protection"), symbolizes the complete and absolute rule of God in one's life, or a deeply devoted and protected servant of God.

historical_references.reference: According to medieval Italian legends, Erminio was a legendary Roman hero who was said to have been the first to introduce Christianity to the region of Emilia-Romagna. He is believed to have been a soldier in the Roman army during the late 3rd century AD, and is said to have been converted to Christianity by St. Peter himself. After his conversion, Erminio reportedly left the army and traveled throughout the region, preaching the Christian faith and performing miracles. He is often depicted as a warrior saint with a palm branch and a labarum, the military standard of the Roman Empire bearing the Chi-Rho monogram.

Another reference to Erminio can be found in the works of the medieval Italian poet Girolamo Cardano. In his poem 'De Proprietatibus Rerum', Cardano mentions a saint named Erminio who was a bishop in the city of Modena during the early Christian period. According to Cardano, Erminio was a wise and just ruler who was beloved by his people. He is said to have built a church in Modena dedicated to St. Peter, and is remembered in local tradition as a patron saint of the city.
